recall.minute: Alignment teaches preferences (helpful, honest, harmless) beyond SFT's imitation; judging is easier than demonstrating. Preference data: (x, y_w, y_l) with guidelines; agreement ~65–80%. Reward model: Bradley–Terry σ(r_w − r_l) (2 vs 1 → 0.73, loss 0.313); relative scores, a proxy. RLHF: PPO maximises r − β·log(π/π_ref) (β = 0.1: 2 with log-ratio 5 → 1.50); clipped updates, critic; four models. DPO: −log σ(β[(log π − log π_ref)(y_w) − (…)(y_l)]); 0.693 at start; two models; offline. GRPO: G samples per prompt, A = (r − mean)/std, no critic, verifiable rewards ([1,0,1,0,0,1,1,0] → ±1). RLAIF/Constitutional AI: AI judge with written principles; self-critique and revision. Risks: reward hacking (length bias), sycophancy, over-refusal, over-optimisation (Goodhart).
